subject: Cloud Computing
title: VPN and Private Connectivity
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on VPN and Private Connectivity.

hook.text: Your office needs a secure link to your cloud. Sending data over the public internet isn't safe enough.

buildup.text: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel between your network and the cloud, hiding traffic from eavesdroppers.

discovery.text: For higher performance, AWS Direct Connect and Azure ExpressRoute provide dedicated physical links.

twist.text: Dedicated links cost thousands per month. Most small companies use VPN instead and accept the trade-off.

climax.text: Private connectivity removes the public internet from the equation. It's slower to set up but much more secure.

punchline.text: VPN is the tunnel. Direct connect is the private highway.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of AWS Direct Connect over a VPN?
options: It provides a dedicated physical connection that bypasses the public internet
It's free for all AWS customers
It doesn't require any network configuration

details.summary: VPNs and dedicated connections like AWS Direct Connect or Azure ExpressRoute create private, encrypted links between on-premises networks and cloud environments. They keep sensitive traffic off the public internet and provide more predictable performance.
details.whyItMatters: Sensitive workloads and regulatory requirements often demand that traffic never traverse the public internet. Private connectivity ensures confidentiality and consistent network performance.
takeaways: VPNs encrypt traffic between on-premises and cloud
Direct connections bypass the public internet entirely
Private links offer lower latency and higher reliability

faq.question: When should you use a VPN vs a direct connection?
faq.answer: VPNs work well for smaller workloads and quick setup over the internet. Direct connections are preferred for high-bandwidth, latency-sensitive, or compliance-driven workloads where predictable performance and dedicated bandwidth are worth the higher cost.

faq.question: Can VPN traffic still be intercepted?
faq.answer: VPN traffic is encrypted, so interception provides only unreadable ciphertext. However, VPN endpoints themselves can be targeted. Keeping VPN software updated, using strong encryption algorithms, and combining VPN with zero trust principles ensures robust protection.
